about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

notStaged.reason: This run predates `tools/mapper stage` (#223). Its inputs were staged by hand and were not committed, so there is nothing to hold to a digest: unlike trials 7 and 8, which each wrote a blind-mapping/REDACTIONS.md, this directory has no record of what the second mapper was given. What can be said is what blind-mapping/README.md says -- the mapper was given the pinned extract and had not seen Map A -- and that rests on the runner's word, which is exactly the gap #223 is about. It is recorded here rather than left blank so that the one blind-second-mapping review this repository currently rests on says out loud that its inputs cannot be checked.

firstMap.note: Map A, the first mapping, and the map these bytes are the correction of. It was this example's corpus-map.json under the `legacy` exemption until the reconciled map was promoted to that name (#8); it is frozen evidence now, beside Map B, and carries no review of its own for the reason Map B carries none -- it is an input to this comparison, not a map this repository uses. It is a file and not only a git object because blind-mapping/build-map-c.py reads it: `--check` rebuilds these bytes from it and the resolutions on every validate.sh run, so a correction nobody ruled on fails the gate, and the digest above is the same one compared.sha256 names.

blindMap.note: Map B, copied verbatim from the mapper's bundle with its corpus-manifest.json, and not edited. It is evidence, not a map this repository uses, so it carries no review of its own and is not named by the glob that requires one.

corpus-map.json.scope: Every disagreement results.json flagged has a ruling in resolutions.json. The last one recorded open, worked-examples-as-entries (#216), was ruled on 2026-09-17 by rules-factory decision 0031 and the row carries that ruling beside its original: these bytes differ from the reviewed ones by that row alone, applied by blind-mapping/build-map-c.py, which validate.sh re-runs. What it adds is short-temporary-absences.ambiguity.bounds -- the two (c)(4) examples the blind second mapping and the adjudication both read, with their citations and their verbatim text, which the locator checker holds to the corpus -- and the question it rewrote no longer re-quotes them. No entry's scope, kind, clarity or fate moved.
